name: ARRAY
desc: Covers the ARRAY expression: array type checks, partial/exact length assertions, positive and negative subset offsets, end boundaries and missing nodes, inherited match modes, explicit sequence terms, nested-array consumption, captures, evaluated operands, and failure propagation. ARRAY does not initiate sequence context, and with element patterns it leaves an unmatched suffix permitted even under IS. Expected results are derived from the specification rather than implementation behavior.

tests.name: Array type checks
tests.desc: With no arguments ARRAY checks only whether the current node exists and is an array. No conversion from strings, objects, null, or booleans is implied.

tests.name: Length assertions
tests.desc: The one-argument form compares array length: HAS requires at least the supplied integer, while IS requires exactly it. Negative integers are valid operands; no array has a negative length, and every array has at least a negative number of elements.

tests.desc: Length checks depend on the array length rather than the types or values of its elements.

tests.name: Subset offsets and literal elements
tests.desc: Offsets count from the start, or from the end when negative. Offsets outside [0,length] fail without errors; a position at length is a missing node rather than null. With patterns both HAS and IS permit an unmatched suffix.

tests.name: Input []
tests.desc: A single literal term is compared at the normalized offset; exact mode does not require matching the rest of the containing array.

Matching mode and structures
tests.desc: ARRAY preserves inherited HAS/IS mode within its element patterns, while always allowing a remaining suffix in the containing array. Nested ARRAY expressions start another array match, and explicit child comparisons may override matching mode.

Evaluated operands and references
tests.desc: The length/offset expression evaluates on the current array before selecting elements. References and common expressions may supply integers or literal patterns without becoming target aliases or being evaluated as syntax twice.

Captures and action scope
tests.desc: Named sequences among ARRAY patterns report absolute offsets in the matched array and retain paths into nested input. Captures are visible to MATCH subactions; ANY/NONE/REP retain their usual suppression behavior.

Invalid operands, laziness, and syntax
tests.desc: Noninteger computed arguments are recoverable operand failures and become false inside matches. Intrinsically invalid literal arguments may be diagnosed as INVALID_GRAFT. Target failures, intentional FAIL, and offset bounds do not become syntax errors. Fatal syntax and resource errors remain fatal.

tests.name: Mismatching earlier pattern skips later failure
False bounds do not validate unused syntax at runtime
Pending array edits
tests.desc: During MOVE, deleted array slots are missing although length and unshifted indices remain unchanged until the action completes. ARRAY length/type checks do not enumerate elements. The equivalent leading EXISTS checks must reject missing prefix elements; exact-mode trailing EXISTS checks reject missing suffix elements, while explicit patterns may match a missing slot. To expose a probe inside MOVE, the final destination selector is arranged to be false (the valid append alias) when the expected boolean is obtained; true would be invalid.
